classificationValues.existing-core: The current stable Core surface already owns the capability.
classificationValues.native-guidance: Native HTML or browser behavior is the preferred public contract.
classificationValues.core-1.1-primitive: A bounded additive primitive is accepted for Core 1.1 after stable 1.0.
classificationValues.later-core-candidate: The capability needs a later decision or platform tranche before implementation.
classificationValues.core-recipe: The capability is best taught as a tested, copyable composition rather than a component API.
classificationValues.adapter: The capability belongs in an optional integration or deterministic interchange layer.
classificationValues.pro: The capability is a reusable product-ready composition or workflow.
classificationValues.consumer-owned: The consuming application owns the policy, data, routing, or one-product composition.
classificationValues.rejected: Nerio intentionally does not plan a dedicated maintained surface.

sequence.rule: Only real manual evidence and the existing stable sequence may change the Core 1.0 release line.
Establish the minimum direction and localization contract first; the full repository audit is a parallel shared track, not a global serialization barrier.
Disclosure, dialog, single-selection, search, OTP, and number work may proceed in parallel after their shared direction decisions are accepted.
Grouped selection and menu anatomy may proceed independently of the field family.
Keep MultiSelect as a decision spike; no implementation is approved by this matrix.
The stable-1.0 recipe tranche and Agent Skill are independent of new primitives; later recipes depend only on the exact components they use.
Package analysis, CLI modularization, MCP discovery, and Lab decisions may run in parallel; Registry namespaces wait only for CLI modularization, and bootstrap waits for the package-output decision.

sequence.mayStart: after the first accepted Core 1.1 tranche
sequence.rule: Code-owned Figma exports may be prepared only against an explicitly frozen component subset; a real file and visual approval remain manual.

issueDispositions.title: Direction, RTL, locale, and localization contract
issueDispositions.decision: Shared foundation, but not a requirement to finish the entire repository audit before every component PR. Each new direction-sensitive API must wait for the relevant accepted contract.

issueDispositions.title: Accordion and Collapsible
issueDispositions.decision: Both responsibilities are durable and distinct; simple disclosure continues to use native details and summary guidance.

issueDispositions.title: Compound Dialog and AlertDialog
issueDispositions.decision: Additive compound anatomy and a separate confirmation responsibility are justified; the current convenience Dialog must remain compatible.

issueDispositions.title: Single-select Combobox
issueDispositions.decision: Accept one synchronous, single-select, form-backed primitive; fetching, creation, virtualization, and product search remain outside Core.

issueDispositions.title: SearchField
issueDispositions.decision: Retain #346 for SearchField only. NumberField has a different value, locale, form, and primitive contract and moves to #370.

issueDispositions.title: OTPField
issueDispositions.decision: Base UI 1.6.0 marks OTPField stable; Core owns one form value, not authentication or verification policy.

issueDispositions.title: ToggleGroup and CheckboxGroup
issueDispositions.decision: Keep one family issue but require independent semantic slices and allow separate PRs; neither waits for the other.

issueDispositions.title: MultiSelect decision spike
issueDispositions.decision: No Core implementation is accepted yet. Re-evaluate after real Combobox and CheckboxGroup use; composition or Pro remains a valid final outcome.

issueDispositions.title: Complete compound DropdownMenu family
issueDispositions.decision: Links, checkbox/radio items, and submenus are additive menu anatomy. ContextMenu, Menubar, and NavigationMenu remain separate non-goals.

issueDispositions.title: Package output decision
issueDispositions.decision: Measure source, compiled, hybrid, and configuration-only options. Compiled output is not predetermined.

issueDispositions.title: CLI lifecycle and bootstrap
issueDispositions.decision: Modularization and source lifecycle can start independently. Project bootstrap waits only for #351.

issueDispositions.title: Namespaced Registries
issueDispositions.decision: Reuse the existing integrity, transport, planning, and transaction engine; wait for the CLI modularization slice, not full bootstrap.

issueDispositions.title: Expanded MCP
issueDispositions.decision: Keep #354 focused on bounded read-only MCP discovery and planning. The repository-native Agent Skill is tracked separately by #369.

issueDispositions.title: Component Lab decision
issueDispositions.decision: Prototype and measure docs-local, Storybook, expanded fixtures, and defer options. Existing visual fixtures remain the default until evidence justifies a new surface.

issueDispositions.title: Bounded Core recipes
issueDispositions.decision: A stable-1.0 tranche may start without Core 1.1; later recipes depend only on their exact accepted components.

issueDispositions.title: Open Core Figma library
issueDispositions.decision: Code-to-Figma export and drift tooling are valid, but the component subset waits for the first Core 1.1 tranche and completion requires a real approved file.

issueDispositions.title: Nerio product-interface Agent Skill
issueDispositions.decision: Use #369 as the canonical skill issue. It may reuse #354 MCP outputs but must not remain duplicated inside the MCP implementation scope.

issueDispositions.title: NumberField
issueDispositions.decision: Independent numeric value and locale contract split from #346.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need one stable visual value layer and runtime appearance contract.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Keep theme, mode, density, and token override contracts synchronized without new runtime axes.

capabilities.userProblem: Consumers need icons and advanced motion without mandatory peer cost.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Keep optional peers isolated and icons behind the Nerio adapter.

capabilities.userProblem: Users need actions, pressed state, and related action grouping.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Preserve action, independent pressed-state, and group responsibilities.

capabilities.userProblem: Forms need native editing plus coherent labels, messages, grouping, and source ownership.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Core owns control and accessible relationships; consumers own validation and submission policy.

capabilities.userProblem: Forms need binary, exclusive, single-select, and one-value range controls.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Preserve distinct control semantics and one owner per value.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need a bounded custom path for one calendar date.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: One ISO date, deterministic initialization, localization hooks, and no scheduling policy.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need modal, side-panel, anchored popup, and contextual help behavior.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Core owns focus, dismissal, layering, and resilient anatomy; consumers own task policy.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need a bounded secondary-command menu.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: The current convenience menu remains stable while #350 adds bounded anatomy.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need semantic surfaces, identity, structured data, lists, and simple metrics.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Static semantic presentation only; data operations and product semantics remain outside Core.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need persistent, transient, loading, empty, and progress feedback.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Core owns presentation and announcement contracts, not task or notification-center policy.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need local navigation, hierarchy, pagination, layout, and command-result primitives.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Core owns primitive behavior and layout; routing, fetching, ranking, and app shell policy remain consumer or Pro responsibilities.

capabilities.userProblem: Consumers need explicit guidance where a wrapper adds no durable value.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Prefer native color input, meter, details/summary, select, output, overflow, links, and landmarks when no shared state machine is needed.

capabilities.userProblem: Components need one inherited direction and deterministic localization contract.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Inherit document direction by default; add a provider or locale prop only where evidence proves inheritance or Intl is insufficient.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need controlled individual and grouped disclosure beyond simple native details.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Collapsible owns one disclosure; Accordion owns a single/multiple group; native details remains documented.

capabilities.userProblem: Consumers need custom dialog anatomy and an explicit confirmation contract.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Preserve the current Dialog API; add meaningful compound parts and a separate conservative confirmation responsibility.

capabilities.userProblem: Long known option sets need filtering plus one selected form value.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: One synchronous selected value with consumer-supplied data and bounded filtering.

capabilities.userProblem: Search input needs a semantic clear action and predictable search events.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: One query input, clear action, and search event composed from existing form primitives.

capabilities.userProblem: Numeric entry needs one locale-aware value and increment/decrement contract.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: One finite numeric form value with deterministic locale, min, max, step, and reset behavior.

capabilities.userProblem: Verification-code entry needs reliable paste, autofill, focus, and one form value.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: One bounded form value with mobile, paste, deletion, and accessible group behavior.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need grouped pressed states and grouped independent checkboxes.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Keep ToggleGroup and CheckboxGroup as separate semantics and independently deliverable slices.

capabilities.userProblem: Long popup option sets may require multiple form values.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Approve only after composition is proven insufficient and selected-value presentation remains bounded.

capabilities.userProblem: Menus need links, selection items, and nested commands without a second abstraction.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Add meaningful Menu parts while keeping the current data-array API compatible.

capabilities.userProblem: Pointer and keyboard users may need commands attached to an object context.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Revisit only after the shared menu family is stable and non-pointer access has clear value.
capabilities.reasonNoIssue: Low frequency and high discoverability/accessibility cost do not justify a current issue.

capabilities.userProblem: Dense editors and sites may need menubars, toolbars, or navigation menus.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Use Button, ToggleGroup, DropdownMenu, links, and product composition until repeated domain-agnostic evidence appears.
capabilities.reasonNoIssue: Current need is product composition rather than one accepted Core responsibility.

capabilities.userProblem: Pointer users sometimes benefit from a preview before navigation.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Use Popover, Tooltip, or product-owned link previews when the content has real value.
capabilities.reasonNoIssue: The primitive encourages low-frequency pointer-first UI and adds no current universal responsibility.

capabilities.userProblem: Free-form input may need optional suggestions without selected-value state.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Teach SearchField or Input plus consumer-owned suggestions; Command remains the action-result primitive.

capabilities.userProblem: Products need date ranges, upload flows, advanced color tools, and complex data controls.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Keep reusable product-ready workflows in Pro and one-product policy in consumers.

capabilities.userProblem: Data-rich products need sorting, filtering, saved views, metrics, and chart context.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Pro owns reusable data workflows; Core Table and Stat remain static primitives.

capabilities.userProblem: Teams need complete application, documentation, finance, AI, and template surfaces.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Pro owns reusable product solutions; templates may keep unproven patterns local.

capabilities.userProblem: Package consumers need the smallest reliable setup without losing source mode.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Choose source, compiled, hybrid, or configuration-only improvements by measured consumer evidence.

capabilities.userProblem: Source consumers need modular, transactional lifecycle and bounded bootstrap tools.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Modularize first, then add independent transactional lifecycle slices; bootstrap follows #351.

capabilities.userProblem: Teams need deterministic public, internal, and future Pro Registry origins.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Reuse existing integrity, transport, planning, transaction, and redaction contracts.

capabilities.userProblem: Agents need bounded canonical capability, source, token, composition, and plan discovery.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Read-only, versioned, bounded tools derive from canonical data and reuse CLI plans where applicable.

capabilities.userProblem: Coding agents need concise Nerio product-interface judgment and validation guidance.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: One canonical progressive-disclosure skill validated against real Nerio paths, APIs, and commands.

capabilities.userProblem: Maintainers may need efficient state-matrix exploration beyond canonical docs.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Existing docs and visual fixtures remain authoritative until a measured prototype proves another surface is worth maintaining.

capabilities.userProblem: Consumers need maintained compositions between primitives and complete product templates.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Recipes are copyable compositions with separate metadata, not stable component identities.
nonGoals: New Core props for recipe convenience

capabilities.userProblem: Design teams need code-owned tokens and component metadata in Figma.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Code remains canonical; completion requires deterministic export plus a real maintainer-approved Figma file.

capabilities.userProblem: Nerio internals need composition helpers, CSP context, and responsive observation.
capabilities.acceptanceBoundary: Consume these only behind a component or application requirement; do not mirror Base UI package utilities as Nerio components.
capabilities.reasonNoIssue: These are implementation utilities or consumer configuration, not user-facing component gaps.
